tail <- qnorm(1 - .05 / 2)
res_comb_$bootstrap_ratio <- original_betas$Value / res_comb_$sd
res_comb_$th_pval <- 2 * pnorm(abs(res_comb_$bootstrap_ratio), lower.tail = FALSE)
res_comb_$th_lower_bound <- original_betas$Value - res_comb_$sd * tail
res_comb_$th_upper_bound <- original_betas$Value + res_comb_$sd * tail

# Directional consistency relative to the original whole-sample coefficient
# Among selected bootstrap coefficients, calculate the proportion that keep
# the same sign as the original whole-sample coefficient.
orig_sign <- sign(original_betas$Value)
n_same_sign_as_original <- matrixStats::rowSums2(
  (sign(val_matrix) == orig_sign) & (val_matrix != 0),
  na.rm = TRUE
)
res_comb_$n_selected <- n_selected
res_comb_$sign_consistency <- ifelse(
  n_selected > 0 & orig_sign != 0,
  n_same_sign_as_original / n_selected,
  NA_real_
)

12 12. THE STABLE HEATMAP: Filtering by Bootstrap Stability

12.1 12.1 Interpretation of the Stable Signature

After passing the selected post-bootstrap filter, only robust associations remain. The heatmap shows:

  • Red cells: Positive associations that survived the stability filter
  • Green cells: Protective associations that survived the stability filter
  • White cells: Either sparse (λ shrunk to zero) OR failed the stability filter

This is a “cleaned” signature. The primary filter is based on selection probability (sel_prob >= 0.90). A stricter version additionally requires directional consistency (sign_consistency >= 0.80) among selected bootstrap coefficients.

# ==============================================================================
# BLOCK 12: UNIVERSAL STABLE HEATMAP GENERATOR
# ==============================================================================
# DESCRIPTION: Generates cleaned heatmaps by masking associations that do not
#              pass the selected post-bootstrap stability criteria.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 12.0 User-defined post-bootstrap filtering thresholds
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two filters are generated:
#
# 1) Selection-stability filter:
#    sel_prob >= sel_prob_threshold
#
# 2) Stricter stability filter:
#    sel_prob >= sel_prob_threshold and
#    sign_consistency >= sign_consistency_threshold
#
# The default values below are practical starting points, not universal rules.
# Lower thresholds may retain more associations; higher thresholds will give a
# more conservative stable signature.

sel_prob_threshold <- 0.90
sign_consistency_threshold <- 0.80

# 12.1 Define the Universal Plotting Function
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_stable_signature <- function(fit_whole, boot_res, X_mat,
                                  scenario_name,
                                  sel_prob_threshold = 0.90,
                                  sign_consistency_threshold = 0.80,
                                  require_sign_consistency = FALSE) {
  
  filter_label <- if(require_sign_consistency) {
    paste0("sel_prob >= ", sel_prob_threshold,
           " & sign_consistency >= ", sign_consistency_threshold)
  } else {
    paste0("sel_prob >= ", sel_prob_threshold)
  }
  
  message(paste0(">>> Generating Stable Heatmap for: ", scenario_name))
  message(paste0("    -> Filter: ", filter_label))
  
  # A. EXTRACT ORIGINAL BETAS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Get the B matrix from the whole sample fit
  B_orig <- fit_whole$B
  rownames(B_orig) <- colnames(X_mat)
  colnames(B_orig) <- colnames(Y_whole)
  
  # B. PREPARE THE SELECTION-PROBABILITY MASK
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  sel_prob_mask <- boot_res %>%
    select(exposure, outcome, sel_prob) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = sel_prob) %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("exposure")
  
  # Align rows and columns with B matrix
  sel_prob_mask <- sel_prob_mask[rownames(B_orig), colnames(B_orig)]
  stability_mask <- as.matrix(sel_prob_mask) >= sel_prob_threshold
  
  # C. ADD DIRECTIONAL CONSISTENCY MASK IF REQUESTED
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  if(require_sign_consistency) {
    sign_consistency_mask <- boot_res %>%
      select(exposure, outcome, sign_consistency) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = sign_consistency) %>%
      tibble::column_to_rownames("exposure")
    
    # Align rows and columns with B matrix
    sign_consistency_mask <- sign_consistency_mask[rownames(B_orig), colnames(B_orig)]
    stability_mask <- stability_mask &
      (as.matrix(sign_consistency_mask) >= sign_consistency_threshold)
  }
  
  stability_mask[is.na(stability_mask)] <- FALSE
  
  # D. APPLY THE FILTER (MASKING)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  B_stable <- B_orig
  B_stable[!stability_mask] <- 0
  
  # E. POST-FILTER CLEANUP
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Remove rows that are entirely zero after masking (cleaner visualization)
  active_rows <- rowSums(B_stable != 0) > 0
  if(sum(active_rows) == 0) {
    message("    ! WARNING: No associations survived the stability filter.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  coef_subset <- B_stable[active_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  
  # F. ROW ANNOTATIONS (Families)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  clean_names <- gsub("_None|_Ter_2|_Ter_3", "", rownames(coef_subset))
  row_info <- vars_info %>% 
    filter(variable_name %in% clean_names) %>%
    distinct(variable_name, .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  df_row_ann <- data.frame(
    Family = row_info$family[match(clean_names, row_info$variable_name)],
    row.names = rownames(coef_subset)
  )
  
  # G. RENDER PHEATMAP
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  p <- pheatmap(
    coef_subset,
    main              = paste0(scenario_name, " (Stable Signature: ", filter_label, ")"),
    color             = custom_colors_pro,          # Defined in Block 8
    breaks            = get_pro_breaks(coef_subset),# Defined in Block 8
    annotation_row    = df_row_ann,
    cluster_cols      = FALSE,
    cluster_rows      = TRUE,
    border_color      = "white",
    fontsize_row      = 8,
    cellwidth         = 30,
    silent            = TRUE
  )
  
  print(p)
}

# 12.2 Generate stable signatures using the two stability filters
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Pregnancy, selection probability only
grid.newpage()
plot_stable_signature(fit_preg_whole, res_preg, X_preg_whole,
                      "Pregnancy",
                      sel_prob_threshold = sel_prob_threshold,
                      sign_consistency_threshold = sign_consistency_threshold,
                      require_sign_consistency = FALSE)

# Pregnancy, selection probability + directional consistency
grid.newpage()
plot_stable_signature(fit_preg_whole, res_preg, X_preg_whole,
                      "Pregnancy",
                      sel_prob_threshold = sel_prob_threshold,
                      sign_consistency_threshold = sign_consistency_threshold,
                      require_sign_consistency = TRUE)

# Childhood, selection probability only
grid.newpage()
plot_stable_signature(fit_child_whole, res_child, X_child_whole,
                      "Childhood",
                      sel_prob_threshold = sel_prob_threshold,
                      sign_consistency_threshold = sign_consistency_threshold,
                      require_sign_consistency = FALSE)

# Childhood, selection probability + directional consistency
grid.newpage()
plot_stable_signature(fit_child_whole, res_child, X_child_whole,
                      "Childhood",
                      sel_prob_threshold = sel_prob_threshold,
                      sign_consistency_threshold = sign_consistency_threshold,
                      require_sign_consistency = TRUE)

# Combined, selection probability only
grid.newpage()
X_comb_whole <- cbind(X_preg_whole, X_child_whole)
plot_stable_signature(fit_comb_whole, res_comb_, X_comb_whole,
                      "Combined",
                      sel_prob_threshold = sel_prob_threshold,
                      sign_consistency_threshold = sign_consistency_threshold,
                      require_sign_consistency = FALSE)

# Combined, selection probability + directional consistency
grid.newpage()
plot_stable_signature(fit_comb_whole, res_comb_, X_comb_whole,
                      "Combined",
                      sel_prob_threshold = sel_prob_threshold,
                      sign_consistency_threshold = sign_consistency_threshold,
                      require_sign_consistency = TRUE)

13 13. INTERPRETATION EXAMPLES: What a Stable Signature Means

13.1 13.1 Red Cell Example

Traffic Noise → ↑ Asthma (Red) - Selected in at least 90% of bootstraps (sel_prob >= 0.90) - If the stricter filter is used, selected coefficients keep the same direction in at least 80% of selected bootstraps (sign_consistency >= 0.80) - Conclusion: Robust evidence of harm

13.2 13.2 White Cell Example (Multiple Interpretations)

Lead → BMI (White) - Originally sparse (λ shrunk to zero): Not selected in discovery - OR selected in fewer than 90% of bootstraps: unstable driver under the default threshold - OR fails the optional directional consistency filter - Conclusion: No robust evidence of association (may be real but below detection threshold)

14 14. METHODOLOGICAL SUMMARY: From P-Hacking to P-Validating

14.1 14.1 The Evolution

Approach Method Problem Solution
Classical Regression OLS (X^T X)^-1 X^T Y P >> N → singular matrix ✗ Fails
P-Hacking Univariate tests + FDR Multiple testing → false positives Reduces but doesn’t eliminate
LASSO Single-run regularization Selection uncertainty in noisy data Unstable selections
msRRR + Stability Selection 500 balanced bootstraps + selection probability/directional consistency ✓ Validates robustness P-VALIDATING

Key Difference: We shift from “Is this p < 0.05?” to “How consistently is this selected across data perturbations?”

15 15. COMPUTATIONAL REQUIREMENTS & Scalability

  • Total Runtime: ~2-4 hours (5-fold CV + 500 bootstraps, 8 cores)
  • Memory: ~4GB (exposome matrices ~1000×200 + bootstraps)
  • Output: 3 stable heatmaps + bootstrap statistics CSV

16 16. FINAL RECOMMENDATIONS

16.0.1 For Publication:

  1. Report the selection probability threshold and any directional consistency filter used
  2. Document the rank and lambda selection—enables replication
  3. Show the bootstrap distribution—demonstrates stability
  4. Include missing data strategy—transparency

16.0.2 For Future Analyses:

  1. Sensitivity analyses: Try different sel_prob thresholds (e.g., 0.90, 0.80, 0.75) and optional directional consistency thresholds
  2. Stratified models: By sex, age groups
  3. Pleiotropy analysis: Which exposures affect multiple outcomes?

17 APPENDIX: Quick Reference

Three-Stage Protocol:

Stage 1: Stratified 80/20 Split (prevent rare disease imbalance)
         ↓
Stage 2: 5-Fold CV on training (optimize rank & lambda)
         ↓
Stage 3: Whole sample refit + 500 bootstrap (maximize power + validate)

Post-bootstrap Stability Filters:

Primary filter:         sel_prob >= 0.90
Optional stricter filter: sign_consistency >= 0.80 among selected bootstraps

Auxiliary metrics such as pval_ratio, pval_corrected, and th_pval are still computed
for reference and sensitivity checks, but the stable heatmaps are generated from
selection probability and optional directional consistency.
